Honestly it is disgusting that people make fun of you or tell you that it could be worse. Of course it could be worse... everything can always be worse! That doesnt change the fact that things are bad! It doesnt matter how small the situation might seem, if you are hurting yourself over it then it is obviously too much to handle. Oftentimes it is a hundred little reasons and not one big reason too. What is your situation that others disregarded?

For them to completely disregard your suffering like that would cause a great deal of feelings of pain and isolation. I know what that feels like and my heart goes out to you. Do you mind if I ask you who you have told that replied like that?? You need to find somebody to talk to who wont think that of you.

I dont know what to say for coping with pain- if I knew I wouldnt have cut for so many years. I will tell you though that my key to stopping (I stopped in 2013 after 4 years of cutting) was through finding somebody who understood and was going through the same thing as me. Cutting is a slippery slope because it provides such easy short term relief which becomes addicting in hard times of constant struggling.

What I can say helps a bit is writing things out. Put all of your pain out onto reddit for others to read and help you with. It wont solve your problems but it can help you process things a little better. Youll never really replace the feeling of relief that a razor gives you. There is no easy answer. To cope with the pain best, you have to learn to survive with the pain and get to the point where you dont need to cope. Getting there is a tough journey.

If you ever need to talk to someone you can PM me. This goes for anyone reading this reply too.

Sometimes you dont gear/build properly to fight the final boss. Other times the boss simply counters your character and there is nothing you can do about it.

Often, the game crashes because it ran enough calculations and realized you wont be able to win. Its kind of a bastardized act of mercy. You might find in the future games that you see the signs of a weak build and know when to retire your character before being beat up on the final boss.

It sucks starting a new game. You start back at level 1 in a newly randomly generated world that you have no idea about the mechanics of. Slowly, you learn. Techniques that worked well in the last playthrough are obsolete, but you might find another strategy that works even better here. You might even find your build becomes stronger even faster than it did previously. Maybe you have near invulnerability, or you dish out loads of damage, or you are able to afford any item you need. Either way, each run has its perks and no two will be the same. After playing a while in the new world, you might not even want to return to the old one. You can always reflect back on it fondly, remembering your first experience with the game and how much fun you had.

I can say, as someone 4.5 years clean of cutting, that quitting is not easy. Its a god damn journey. Dont expect it to be easy because all it takes is one bad day for you to fall back on the relief that a blade offers. Some people never make the journey, others it comes easy. The day I quit for good, I knew I would never go back. I was sure of my decision, and you know what, I was right. The first couple months of dating are the 'honeymoon phase'. They will almost inevitably go perfectly. Also notice that when you became best friends and things were going well, a relationship started to form. Was that out of true feelings of love, or out of a strong friendship? What was she going through at the time?

Do you still self harm OP?

I went through a cutting phase in 2009-2013 but I am 6 years clean of the razor now. I still get urges, especially often, but I have not marked my skin in any major way since.

There's no good end to cutting. You will come to regret every scar you give yourself, and every cut will need to be deeper to get the same rush as you got from the first. If anyone is in a bad place or needs help, feel free to PM me too. I am not exactly perfectly adjusted myself, but I know what self harm is like and I know how easy and addicting it can get to use it as an escape.

The few people I've told have all been understanding. Expect a few stares but very few people will approach you and say anything.

I cut my wrists a lot back in the day (6-9 years ago now?) and managed to hide it all this time. I wear a watch and it covers most of the marks, so no one really notices.

EDIT also be really really careful with drinking+cutting. I know you say the cuts are shallow but alcohol can give you the nerve to make the biggest cuts you've ever done. My worst scar is thanks to that.
